articles.title: Upper density of a packing
articles.statement:
For a packing $P$ of congruent balls in $\mathbb{R}^4$, let
$U_P$ be the union of the closed balls of the packing, and for $p \in \mathbb{R}^4$ and $R > 0$ let
$B(p, R)$ be the open ball of radius $R$ about $p$. The upper density of $P$ is the extended
nonnegative real number

$$\limsup_{R \to \infty} \sup_{p \in \mathbb{R}^4}
\frac{\operatorname{vol}(U_P \cap B(p, R))}{\operatorname{vol}(B(p, R))},$$

where $\operatorname{vol}$ is Lebesgue measure and the limit superior is taken as the positive
radius $R$ tends to infinity.

## Sources

- CE2003 Appendix A, limsup as positive radii tend to infinity.

articles.title: Manifolds admitting a metric of positive scalar curvature
articles.statement:
A smooth manifold $M$ without
boundary modeled on $\mathbb{R}^n$ admits a metric of positive scalar curvature when some
$C^\infty$ Riemannian metric $g$ on its tangent bundle has scalar curvature, computed for $g$,
strictly positive at every point of $M$.

articles.title: Conformal class of a Riemannian metric
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on a
real normed space, and let $g$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric on $M$, with inner product $g_x$
on the tangent space $T_x M$. The conformal class of $g$ is the set of $C^\infty$ Riemannian
metrics $g'$ on $M$ for which there is a $C^\infty$ function $u : M \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$u(x) > 0$ for all $x \in M$ and $g'_x(v, w) = u(x)\, g_x(v, w)$ for all $x \in M$ and all
$v, w \in T_x M$.

articles.title: Inner product of a conformally scaled metric
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a
manifold $B$, let $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian
metric on $E$, with inner product $g_b$ on the fiber $E_b$, and let $u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a
$C^n$ function with $u(b) > 0$ for every $b \in B$. Then the conformal scaling $u g$ of $g$ by
$u$ satisfies $(u g)_b(v, w) = u(b)\, g_b(v, w)$ for every $b \in B$ and all $v, w \in E_b$.

articles.title: Conformal scalings lie in the conformal class
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled
on a real normed space, let $g$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric on $M$, and let
$u : M \to \mathbb{R}$ be a $C^\infty$ function with $u(x) > 0$ for all $x \in M$. Then the
conformal scaling $u g$ of $g$ by $u$ lies in the conformal class of $g$.

articles.title: Conformal scaling of a Riemannian metric
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a
manifold $B$, let $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian
metric on $E$, and let $u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a $C^n$ function with $u(b) > 0$ for every
$b \in B$. The conformal scaling of $g$ by $u$ is the $C^n$ Riemannian metric $u g$ on $E$
whose inner product on each fiber $E_b$ is $u(b)$ times the inner product of $g$ on $E_b$.

articles.title: Conformal metrics via an exponential factor
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on
a real normed space, and let $g$ and $g'$ be $C^\infty$ Riemannian metrics on $M$, with inner
products $g_x$ and $g'_x$ on the tangent space $T_x M$. Then $g'$ lies in the conformal class of
$g$ if and only if there is a $C^\infty$ function $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g'_x(v, w) = e^{f(x)}\, g_x(v, w)$ for all $x \in M$ and all $v, w \in T_x M$.

articles.title: Conformal equivalence is symmetric
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on a real
normed space, and let $g$ and $g'$ be $C^\infty$ Riemannian metrics on $M$. If $g'$ lies in the
conformal class of $g$, then $g$ lies in the conformal class of $g'$.

articles.title: Conformal equivalence is transitive
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on a real
normed space, and let $g$, $g'$ and $g''$ be $C^\infty$ Riemannian metrics on $M$. If $g'$ lies
in the conformal class of $g$ and $g''$ lies in the conformal class of $g'$, then $g''$ lies in
the conformal class of $g$.

articles.title: Lowering the smoothness keeps the inner product
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a
manifold $B$, let $m \le n$ be smoothness exponents in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, and
let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian metric on $E$. For every $b \in B$, the inner product on the fiber
$E_b$ of $g$ viewed as a $C^m$ Riemannian metric equals the inner product of $g$ on $E_b$.

articles.title: Lowering the smoothness of a Riemannian metric
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a
manifold $B$, let $m \le n$ be smoothness exponents in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, and
let $g$ be a $C^n$ Riemannian metric on $E$. Then $g$, with the same inner product on every
fiber, is a $C^m$ Riemannian metric on $E$.

articles.title: A conformal factor at a point is positive
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector bundle over a
manifold $B$, let $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty, \omega\}$, and let $g$ and $g'$ be $C^n$
Riemannian metrics on $E$, with inner products $g_b$ and $g'_b$ on the fiber $E_b$. Let
$u : B \to \mathbb{R}$ and $b \in B$. If $g'_b(v, w) = u(b)\, g_b(v, w)$ for all $v, w \in E_b$
and $E_b$ contains a nonzero vector, then $u(b) > 0$.

articles.title: A metric lies in its own conformal class
articles.statement:
Every smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on a
smooth manifold $M$ lies in the conformal class of $g$.

articles.title: Antisymmetry of the curvature expression
articles.statement:
For every covariant derivative $\nabla$ on a
vector bundle $V$ over a manifold $M$, every $x \in M$, all $u, v \in T_x M$ and every
$\sigma \in V_x$, the curvature expression $R$ of $\nabla$ on extensions satisfies
$R(u, v)\sigma = -R(v, u)\sigma$.

articles.title: Curvature expression of a covariant derivative on extensions
articles.statement:
Let $\nabla$ be a covariant
derivative on a vector bundle $V$ over a manifold $M$, let $x \in M$, let $u, v \in T_x M$ and let
$\sigma \in V_x$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be the vector fields on $M$ whose coordinates in the preferred
local trivialization of $TM$ at $x$ are constant, equal to those of $u$ and $v$, on the base set
of that trivialization, with a fixed but unspecified value at each point outside it; let $S$ be
the section of $V$ obtained in the same way from $\sigma$ and the preferred local trivialization
of $V$ at $x$. The curvature expression of $\nabla$ at $x$ on $u$, $v$, $\sigma$ is the vector

$$R(u, v)\sigma = \nabla_u (\nabla_Y S) - \nabla_v (\nabla_X S) - \nabla_{[X, Y](x)} S \in V_x,$$

where $\nabla_Y S$ is the section $y \mapsto \nabla_{Y(y)} S$ and $[X, Y]$ is the Lie bracket.

When $\nabla$ sends $C^2$ sections to $C^1$ sections (for instance the Levi-Civita connection of a
$C^\infty$ metric), this is the curvature tensor
$R(X, Y) = \nabla_X \nabla_Y - \nabla_Y \nabla_X - \nabla_{[X, Y]}$ applied to $u$, $v$, $\sigma$,
and it does not depend on the extensions. For other connections it can depend on values of
$\nabla$ that the axioms of a covariant derivative leave unconstrained.

articles.title: Extending a tangent vector of a normed space gives a constant vector field
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself, so that
each tangent space of $F$ is $F$. For every point $x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point
$y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the
tangent bundle at $x$) has value $u$ at $y$.

articles.title: Ricci contraction of the curvature expression
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a manifold modelled on a
finite-dimensional normed space over a nontrivially normed field $\mathbb{K}$, let $\nabla$ be a
covariant derivative on the tangent bundle of $M$, let $R$ be its curvature expression on
extensions, let $x \in M$ and let $v, w \in T_x M$. With $e_1, \dots, e_n$ the fixed basis of
$T_x M$ chosen for every finite-dimensional space and $e_1^*, \dots, e_n^*$ its coordinate
functionals, the Ricci contraction is

$$\operatorname{Ric}(v, w) = \sum_{i=1}^n e_i^*(R(e_i, v) w) \in \mathbb{K},$$

the trace of $z \mapsto R(z, v) w$ computed in that basis (Lang, *Lecture Notes on Riemannian
Geometry*, Def. 2.7). No metric is involved.

When $z \mapsto R(z, v) w$ is linear, as it is for a connection that sends $C^2$ sections to $C^1$
sections, this is its trace and does not depend on the basis.

articles.title: Einstein metric
articles.statement:
A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ is Einstein when there is a real
constant $\lambda$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, w) = \lambda \, g_x(v, w)$ for every point
$x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci
curvature ([Lang], Einstein manifolds). Ricci-flat is the case $\lambda = 0$.

articles.title: The Levi-Civita connection of Euclidean space kills constant vector fields
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product
on every tangent space, and let $\nabla$ be its Levi-Civita connection. For every point $x \in F$
and tangent vector $w \in T_xF$, let $W$ be the extension of $w$ to a vector field on $F$ (built
from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$; it is the constant vector field with value
$w$). Then the covariant derivative $\nabla W$ at every point $y \in F$ is the zero map.

articles.title: Extensions of tangent vectors of a normed space are differentiable
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normed
space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For every point
$x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point $y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field
on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$), viewed as a map from $F$ to
its tangent bundle, is differentiable at $y$, not only at the base point $x$.

articles.title: Lie brackets of extended tangent vectors of a normed space vanish
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normed
space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For points
$x, x' \in F$ and tangent vectors $a \in T_xF$ and $b \in T_{x'}F$, let $X$ and $Y$ be the
extensions of $a$ and $b$ to vector fields on $F$ (built from the trivializations of the tangent
bundle at $x$ and at $x'$). Then the Lie bracket $[X, Y]$ vanishes at every point $y \in F$.

articles.title: Ricci curvature bounded below
articles.statement:
A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ has Ricci curvature
at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$, written $\operatorname{Ric} \ge k g$, when
$\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, v) \ge k \|v\|^2$ for every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector
$v \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature and $\|v\|$ is the norm of $v$
given by $g$.

articles.title: Euclidean space is Ricci-flat
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space
with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point
$x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_xF$, the Ricci curvature $\mathrm{Ric}(v, w)$ of $F$
at $x$ is $0$.

articles.title: Ricci curvature
articles.statement:
For a point $x$ of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ and tangent
vectors $v, w \in T_x M$, the Ricci curvature is
$\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, w) = \sum_i e_i^*(R(e_i, v) w)$, where $R$ is the Riemann curvature
endomorphism of the Levi-Civita connection of $g$, $(e_i)$ is a fixed basis of $T_x M$ and
$(e_i^*)$ is its dual basis; the contraction itself uses no metric. Since $z \mapsto R(z, v) w$ is
linear, this is its trace and does not depend on the basis ([Lang, Def. 2.7]). The unit
$n$-sphere has $\operatorname{Ric} = (n - 1) g$.

articles.title: Antisymmetry of the Riemann curvature
articles.statement:
Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold.
Its Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ is antisymmetric in its first two arguments:
$R(u, v) w = -R(v, u) w$ for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_x M$.

articles.title: Euclidean space is flat
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the
Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$
and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_xF$, the Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ of $F$ at $x$
satisfies $R(u, v)w = 0$.

articles.title: Riemann curvature endomorphism
articles.statement:
For a point $x$ of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$
with Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, and tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_x M$,

$$R(u, v) w = (\nabla_X \nabla_Y W - \nabla_Y \nabla_X W - \nabla_{[X, Y]} W)(x),$$

where $X$, $Y$, $W$ are the vector fields extending $u$, $v$, $w$ that have constant coordinates
in the preferred chart at $x$. Since the Levi-Civita connection of a $C^\infty$ metric is
$C^\infty$, this is the textbook curvature endomorphism and does not depend on the extensions.

This is the sign convention of [Lang, Def. 2.1] and [Gud, Def. 8.8]; the opposite sign convention
is also common.

articles.title: Scalar curvature bounded below
articles.statement:
A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has scalar curvature at
least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when its scalar curvature at every point $x \in M$ is at least $k$.

articles.title: Euclidean space has zero scalar curvature
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner
product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For
every point $x \in F$, the scalar curvature of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.

articles.title: Scalar curvature
articles.statement:
The scalar curvature of a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ at a
point $x$ is $\sum_i \operatorname{Ric}_x(e_i, e_i)$, the metric trace of the Ricci curvature
$\operatorname{Ric}$, where $(e_i)$ is a fixed orthonormal basis of $T_x M$ ([Gud, Def. 8.32]).
The unit $n$-sphere has scalar curvature $n (n - 1)$.

articles.title: Sectional curvature bounded below
articles.statement:
A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional
curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \ge k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all
linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature
of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.

articles.title: Sectional curvature bounded above
articles.statement:
A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional
curvature at most $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \le k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all
linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature
of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.

articles.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on equal vectors
articles.statement:
For every point $x$ of a $C^\infty$
Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ and every tangent vector $u \in T_x M$, the sectional curvature formula
$K$ gives $K(u, u) = 0$: its denominator $\|u\|^2 \|u\|^2 - \langle u, u \rangle^2$ vanishes, where
$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and $\|\cdot\|$ are the inner product and norm on $T_x M$ given by
$g$, and a quotient by $0$ is taken to be $0$.

articles.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on a vector and a multiple of it
articles.statement:
Let $(M, g)$ be a
$C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real space (boundary and corners
allowed), and let $x \in M$, $u \in T_x M$ and $c \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the sectional curvature
at $x$ satisfies $K(u, cu) = 0$: the denominator $\|u\|^2 \|cu\|^2 - \langle u, cu \rangle^2$ of
its defining formula vanishes, and the quotient is then $0$ by definition.

articles.title: Euclidean space has zero sectional curvature
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner
product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For
every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xF$, the sectional curvature $K(u, v)$
of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.

articles.title: Sectional curvature
articles.statement:
Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold modeled on a
finite-dimensional real space (boundary and corners allowed), with Riemann curvature
endomorphism $R$, and let $x \in M$. The sectional curvature of tangent vectors
$u, v \in T_x M$ is

$$K(u, v) = \frac{\langle R(u, v) v, u \rangle}{\|u\|^2 \|v\|^2 - \langle u, v \rangle^2},$$

the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$ when they are linearly independent
([Lang, Def. 2.4], [Gud, Def. 8.14]). When $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent the denominator
vanishes and $K(u, v)$ is $0$ by definition.

With the sign convention used here for $R$, the round unit sphere has $K = 1$.

articles.title: Forward Finsler distance
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a Finsler metric on a manifold $M$. The forward
Finsler distance from $x \in M$ to $y \in M$ is the value in $[0, \infty]$

$$
d_F(x, y) = \inf_\gamma \int_0^1 F(\gamma(t), \gamma'(t))\, dt,
$$

the infimum over all $C^1$ paths $\gamma : [0, 1] \to M$ from $x$ to $y$; it is $\infty$ when
there is no such path.

It is not symmetric unless $F$ is reversible.

## Sources

- Bao–Chern–Shen, *An Introduction to Riemann–Finsler Geometry*, §6.2. The formula is that of Mathlib's `riemannianEDist` with `‖v‖ₑ` replaced by `F v`.

articles.title: The Euclidean Finsler metric is reversible
articles.statement:
For every finite-dimensional real inner
product space $V$, the Euclidean Finsler metric $F(x, v) = \|v\|$ on $V$ is reversible:
$F(x, -v) = F(x, v)$ for all $x, v \in V$.

articles.title: Euclidean Finsler metric
articles.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space,
viewed as a smooth manifold whose tangent spaces are $V$ itself. The Euclidean Finsler metric on
$V$ is $F(x, v) = \|v\|$ for $x \in V$ and $v \in T_xV = V$.

articles.title: Finsler metric
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold (possibly with boundary or corners)
modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space $E$, so that each tangent space $T_xM$ is $E$.
A $C^\infty$ Finsler metric on $M$ is a continuous function $F : TM \to \mathbb{R}$ that is
$C^\infty$ off the zero section, satisfies $F(x, v) > 0$ for every $x \in M$ and every nonzero
$v \in T_xM$, is positively homogeneous of degree one on each fiber, that is
$F(x, cv) = c\,F(x, v)$ for all $x \in M$, $v \in T_xM$ and real $c > 0$, and is strongly convex:
for every $x \in M$ and all nonzero $v, w \in E$, the second derivative at $v$ of the function
$u \mapsto F(x, u)^2$ on $E$ satisfies $D^2\big(F(x, \cdot)^2\big)(v)(w, w) > 0$.

## Sources

- Bao–Chern–Shen, *An Introduction to Riemann–Finsler Geometry*, §1.1, where $F$ takes values in $[0, \infty)$ and the Hessian is that of $F^2/2$.

articles.title: Closed Finsler geodesic
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a Finsler metric on a manifold $M$. A curve
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ is a closed geodesic of $F$ if it is a geodesic of $F$, it is periodic
with some period $T > 0$, that is $\gamma(t + T) = \gamma(t)$ for all real $t$, and it is not
constant: $\gamma(t_1) \ne \gamma(t_2)$ for some real $t_1, t_2$.

articles.title: Finsler geodesic of given speed on a set of times
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a Finsler metric on a
manifold $M$ with forward distance $d_F$, let $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ be a curve, let
$s \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set of times and let $c \ge 0$ be a real number. Then $\gamma$ is a
geodesic of speed $c$ of $F$ on $s$ if for every $t \in s$ there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$d_F(\gamma(t_1), \gamma(t_2)) = c\,(t_2 - t_1)$ for all $t_1, t_2 \in s$ with $t_1 \le t_2$,
$|t_1 - t| < \varepsilon$ and $|t_2 - t| < \varepsilon$.

articles.title: Finsler geodesic
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a Finsler metric on a manifold $M$. A curve
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ is a geodesic of $F$ if there is a real number $c \ge 0$ such that
$\gamma$ is a geodesic of speed $c$ of $F$ on all of $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Reversible Finsler metric
articles.statement:
A Finsler metric $F$ on a manifold $M$ is reversible if
$F(x, -v) = F(x, v)$ for every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v \in T_xM$.

articles.title: The geodesic flow of Euclidean space is the straight-line flow
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given
by its inner product, and identify each tangent space of $F$ with $F$, so that a point of the
tangent bundle $TF$ is a pair $(x, v)$ with $x, v \in F$. A family of maps
$\varphi_t \colon TF \to TF$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is a geodesic flow on $TF$ if and only if
$\varphi_t(x, v) = (x + t v, v)$ for every real $t$ and every $(x, v) \in TF$.

articles.title: Geodesic flow on the tangent bundle
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^2$ manifold (boundary and corners
allowed) modeled on a finite-dimensional real space, with a $C^1$ Riemannian metric $g$. A
family of maps $\varphi_t : TM \to TM$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is a geodesic flow of $g$ when
$\varphi_0(v) = v$ for every $v \in TM$, $\varphi_{t+s}(v) = \varphi_t(\varphi_s(v))$ for all
$t, s \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in TM$, and for every $v \in TM$ the orbit $t \mapsto \varphi_t(v)$
is a geodesic velocity curve. Then $\varphi_t(v) = \gamma_v'(t)$ for a geodesic $\gamma_v$ with
initial velocity $v$.

The definition characterizes the flow and does not assert that one exists or is unique. For a
$C^\infty$ metric on a boundaryless manifold, uniqueness is classical, and the global flow exists
when the metric is also complete. No continuity, smoothness or conservation of speed is assumed.

articles.title: Geodesic velocity curves in Euclidean space
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner
product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and
identify each tangent space of $F$ with $F$, so that a point of the tangent bundle $TF$ is a pair
$(x, v)$ with $x, v \in F$. A curve $t \mapsto u(t) = (x(t), v(t))$ in $TF$, defined for all real
$t$, is the velocity curve of a geodesic if and only if, for every real $t$,
$x(t) = x(0) + t\,v(0)$ and $v(t) = v(0)$.

articles.title: Geodesic velocity curves
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^2$ manifold (boundary and corners allowed)
modeled on a finite-dimensional real space, with a $C^1$ Riemannian metric
$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. A curve
$u : \mathbb{R} \to TM$, with base curve $\gamma$ ($\gamma(t)$ is the base point of $u(t)$), is a
geodesic velocity curve when for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$: $\gamma$ is differentiable at $t$ with
velocity $\gamma'(t) = u(t)$; and for every vector field $W$ on $M$ that is differentiable at
$\gamma(t)$, the function $s \mapsto \langle u(s), W(\gamma(s)) \rangle$ has derivative
$\langle u(t), \nabla_{u(t)} W \rangle$ at $t$.

The second condition is the weak form of the geodesic equation $\nabla_{\gamma'} \gamma' = 0$:
by metric compatibility, $\frac{d}{dt} \langle \gamma', W \circ \gamma \rangle =
\langle \nabla_{\gamma'} \gamma', W \rangle + \langle \gamma', \nabla_{\gamma'} W \rangle$, and the
values $W(\gamma(t))$ exhaust the tangent space. The two conditions force $\gamma$ to be $C^2$ in
charts, where the weak form is equivalent to $\nabla_{\gamma'} \gamma' = 0$; no further
smoothness of the curve is assumed.

articles.title: The unit geodesic flow of Euclidean space is the straight-line flow
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given
by its inner product, and identify each tangent space of $F$ with $F$, so that a point of the
tangent bundle is a pair $(x, v)$ with $x, v \in F$, and the unit tangent bundle $SF$ consists of
the pairs with $\|v\| = 1$. A family of maps $\varphi_t \colon SF \to SF$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is
a geodesic flow on $SF$ if and only if $\varphi_t(x, v) = (x + t v, v)$ for every real $t$ and
every $(x, v) \in SF$.

articles.title: Geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^2$ manifold (boundary and
corners allowed) modeled on a finite-dimensional real space, with a $C^1$ Riemannian metric $g$
and unit tangent bundle $SM$. A family of maps $\varphi_t : SM \to SM$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is a
geodesic flow on $SM$ when $\varphi_0(v) = v$ for every $v \in SM$,
$\varphi_{t+s}(v) = \varphi_t(\varphi_s(v))$ for all $t, s \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in SM$, and
for every $v \in SM$ the orbit $t \mapsto \varphi_t(v)$, viewed as a curve in $TM$, is a
geodesic velocity curve. This is the geodesic flow $\varphi_t$ on $SM$ of Burns–Matveev §1:
the orbit of $v$ is the velocity curve of a unit-speed geodesic $\gamma_v$ with initial
velocity $v$.

The definition characterizes the flow and does not assert that one exists or is unique. For a
$C^\infty$ metric on a boundaryless manifold, uniqueness is classical, and the global flow exists
when the metric is also complete. No continuity, smoothness or conservation of speed is assumed.

articles.title: Unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold
articles.statement:
The unit tangent bundle `SM` of a Riemannian manifold `(M, g)`: the tangent vectors whose
norm for the installed metric on their fiber is `1`, as a set of `TangentBundle I M` with the
subspace topology. Source: Burns-Matveev, ETDS 41 (2021), §1 ("the unit tangent bundle ... is
denoted by SM").

articles.title: Hopf–Rinow theorem
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected, locally compact smooth manifold without
boundary, modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, with a smooth Riemannian metric
whose Riemannian distance is the (extended) distance of $M$. Then $M$ is geodesically complete
if and only if $M$ is complete for its distance.

## Sources

- H. Hopf and W. Rinow, *Ueber den Begriff der vollständigen differentialgeometrischen Fläche*, Comment. Math. Helv. 3 (1931), 209-225. Listed as §93 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `hopf_rinow` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Constant-speed geodesic in a metric space
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be an extended metric space with
distance $d$. A path $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ is a constant-speed geodesic if there is a real
number $c \ge 0$ such that every $t_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ has a $\delta > 0$ with
$d(\gamma(s), \gamma(t)) = c\,|t - s|$ for all real $s, t$ with $|s - t_0| < \delta$ and
$|t - t_0| < \delta$.

articles.title: Geodesically complete metric space
articles.statement:
An extended metric space $M$ with distance $d$ is
geodesically complete if the following holds for all real numbers $a < b$ and every path
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$. Suppose there is a real $c \ge 0$ such that every
$t_0 \in (a, b)$ has a $\delta > 0$ with $d(\gamma(s), \gamma(t)) = c\,|t - s|$ for all $s, t$
in the interval $(a, b) \cap (t_0 - \delta, t_0 + \delta)$. Then there is a constant-speed
geodesic $\tilde\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$ with $\tilde\gamma(t) = \gamma(t)$ for all
$t \in (a, b)$.

articles.title: Sum of Killing fields
articles.statement:
On a smooth Riemannian manifold, the sum $X + Y$ of two Killing
vector fields $X$ and $Y$ is a Killing vector field.

articles.title: Real multiples of Killing fields
articles.statement:
On a smooth Riemannian manifold, if $X$ is a Killing
vector field and $c$ is a real number, then $c X$ is a Killing vector field.

articles.title: Extensionality for Killing fields
articles.statement:
Two elements $a$ and $b$ of the space of
Killing vector fields on a smooth Riemannian manifold $M$ that agree at every point
$x \in M$ are equal.

articles.title: Killing's equation on the diagonal
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a Killing vector field on a smooth
Riemannian manifold $M$ with Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. Then
$\langle \nabla_u X, u \rangle = 0$ for every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector
$u \in T_x M$: a Killing field preserves lengths infinitesimally.

articles.title: Killing fields via the diagonal of Killing's equation
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Riemannian
manifold with Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. A vector field $X$ on $M$ is a Killing vector
field if and only if $X$ is smooth and $\langle \nabla_u X, u \rangle = 0$ for every point
$x \in M$ and every tangent vector $u \in T_x M$.

The converse direction is a polarization argument.

articles.title: Killing fields are those with vanishing Lie derivative of the metric
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth
Riemannian manifold with metric $g = \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$. A vector field $X$ on $M$ is
a Killing vector field if and only if $X$ is smooth and, for every point $x \in M$ and all vector
fields $Y$ and $Z$ on $M$ that are differentiable at $x$,

$$X_x \langle Y, Z \rangle - \langle [X, Y]_x, Z_x \rangle - \langle Y_x, [X, Z]_x \rangle = 0,$$

where $X_x \langle Y, Z \rangle$ is the derivative at $x$ of the function
$y \mapsto \langle Y_y, Z_y \rangle$ in the direction $X_x$, and $[X, Y]$ is the Lie bracket.
The left-hand side is $(L_X g)(Y, Z)$ at $x$, where $L_X g$ is the Lie derivative of $g$ along
$X$.

articles.title: The zero field is Killing
articles.statement:
On a smooth Riemannian manifold, the zero vector field is a
Killing vector field.

articles.title: Killing vector field
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, possibly with
boundary or corners, with a smooth Riemannian metric $g = \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and its
Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. A vector field $X$ on $M$ is a Killing vector field if $X$ is
smooth and satisfies Killing's equation: for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors
$u, v \in T_x M$,

$$\langle \nabla_u X, v \rangle + \langle u, \nabla_v X \rangle = 0.$$

In index notation this is $\nabla_i X_j + \nabla_j X_i = 0$, and it is equivalent to the
vanishing of the Lie derivative $L_X g$ of the metric. Smoothness is part of the definition, as
in the textbook definition.

## Sources

- Burns and Matveev (2021), §10.2, for motivation: a Killing field $V$ gives the linear first integral $\xi \mapsto g(V, \xi)$ of geodesic flow.

articles.title: Space of Killing vector fields
articles.statement:
For a smooth Riemannian manifold $M$, the Killing vector
fields on $M$ form a real linear subspace of the real vector space of all (not necessarily
continuous) vector fields on $M$.

articles.title: Membership in the space of Killing fields
articles.statement:
A vector field $X$ on a smooth Riemannian
manifold $M$ lies in the space of Killing vector fields on $M$ if and only if $X$ is a Killing
vector field.

articles.title: The Lie derivative of the metric via the Levi-Civita connection
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth
manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real normed space (possibly with corners), with a smooth
Riemannian metric $g = \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, and let
$X$, $Y$, $Z$ be vector fields on $M$ that are differentiable at a point $x$. Write $[\cdot, \cdot]$
for the Lie bracket of vector fields and $X_x \langle Y, Z \rangle$ for the derivative at $x$ of
the function $y \mapsto \langle Y_y, Z_y \rangle$ in the direction $X_x$. Then

$$
X_x \langle Y, Z \rangle - \langle [X, Y]_x, Z_x \rangle - \langle Y_x, [X, Z]_x \rangle
= \langle \nabla_{Y_x} X, Z_x \rangle + \langle Y_x, \nabla_{Z_x} X \rangle.
$$

The left-hand side is $(\mathcal{L}_X g)(Y, Z)$ at $x$.

articles.title: Translations are Killing
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space,
viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product. For every $c \in F$,
the constant vector field $y \mapsto c$ on $F$ is Killing.

articles.title: Linear Killing fields on Euclidean space
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner
product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and let
$A \colon F \to F$ be a continuous linear map. The linear vector field $y \mapsto A y$ is Killing
if and only if $A$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle A u, w \rangle + \langle u, A w \rangle = 0$ for all
$u, w \in F$.

articles.title: Killing fields on Euclidean space
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product
space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product. A vector field
$V$ on $F$ is Killing if and only if $V$ is $C^\infty$ and its derivative is skew-adjoint at every
point: for all $x, u, w \in F$, $\langle DV(x)\,u, w \rangle + \langle u, DV(x)\,w \rangle = 0$.

articles.title: Laplacian of the Gaussian potential
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product
space of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian metric. For every real number $a$ and every
$x \in F$, the Laplacian of the function $y \mapsto \frac{a}{2}\|y\|^2$ at $x$ is $a \cdot n$.

This function is the potential of the Gaussian gradient Ricci soliton; each diagonal entry of
its Hessian in an orthonormal basis is $a$.

articles.title: Laplacian of the squared norm
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space
of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian metric. For every $x \in F$, the Laplacian of the
function $y \mapsto \|y\|^2$ at $x$ is $2n$.

The Hessian of $\|\cdot\|^2$ is $2\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$, so each of its diagonal entries
in an orthonormal basis is $2$.

articles.title: The Laplacian on a vector space is the flat Laplacian at twice-differentiable points
articles.statement:
Let
$F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with its standard Riemannian metric, let
$f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in F$, and let $Df$ denote the Fréchet derivative of $f$, taken to
be $0$ at points where $f$ is not differentiable. Suppose $Df$ is differentiable at $x$, with
derivative $D^2 f(x)$ there. Then the Laplacian $\Delta f(x)$ equals $\sum_i D^2 f(x)(b_i, b_i)$
for any orthonormal basis $(b_i)$ of $F$, the flat Laplacian of $f$ at $x$.

Without the hypothesis the two can differ: $D^2 f(x)$ is taken to be $0$ when $Df$ is not
differentiable at $x$, while $\Delta f(x)$ is the sum, over the vectors $v$ of the orthonormal
basis used in its definition, of the derivative at $x$ in direction $v$ of the function
$y \mapsto Df(y)(v)$.

articles.title: Laplacian on a vector space as a sum of second directional derivatives
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian
metric, let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in F$, and let $e_1, \dots, e_n$ be the orthonormal
basis of the tangent space $T_xF$ used in the definition of the Laplacian, viewed as vectors of
$F$. For each $i$ let $g_i(y) = Df(y)(e_i)$, where $D$ denotes the Fréchet derivative. Then the
Laplacian of $f$ at $x$ is $\Delta f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} Dg_i(x)(e_i)$. No differentiability of
$f$ is assumed; a Fréchet derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$.

When $Df$ is differentiable at $x$, the right side is the flat Laplacian
$\sum_i D^2 f(x)(e_i, e_i)$ of $f$ at $x$.

articles.title: Laplace–Beltrami operator
articles.statement:
The Laplace-Beltrami operator applied to `f : M → ℝ` at `x`: `Δf(x)` is the metric
trace `∑ i, hessian I f x (e i) (e i)` over the orthonormal basis
`e = stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (TangentSpace I x)`, the same basis convention as
`Manifold.scalarCurvature`. For the textbook Hessian, which is bilinear, this trace
does not depend on the orthonormal basis; the regularity caveat of `Manifold.hessian`
applies here unchanged.

Sign convention `Δf = tr_g ∇²f`, the convention `Δ = div ∘ grad` under which `Δ` is the
sum `∑ ∂²/∂x_i²` on Euclidean space and `Δ(‖x‖²) = 2n`; the operator `-Δ` is then the
nonnegative one, and the opposite sign convention is also common. Reference with the
same conventions: Lee, Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds (2nd ed., GTM 176).

Mathlib's flat Laplacian is `Laplacian.laplacian` (instance
`InnerProductSpace.instLaplacian`, notation `Δ` after `open Laplacian`): the trace of
the second derivative over an orthonormal basis of a finite-dimensional real inner
product space. On the model space `𝓘(ℝ, F)`, under
`DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x`, this operator agrees with Mathlib's `Δ`
(same orthonormal-basis trace, same sign); see `laplacian_vectorSpace_eq_laplacian`
for the proved agreement. What is new here is the manifold operator itself.

articles.title: Metric-compatible covariant derivative
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with
corners) modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, with a smooth Riemannian metric
$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ on its tangent bundle. A covariant derivative $\nabla$ on the
tangent bundle is compatible with the metric if for all smooth vector fields $Y, Z$ on $M$,
every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v \in T_x M$,

$$
v \langle Y, Z \rangle = \langle \nabla_v Y, Z(x) \rangle + \langle Y(x), \nabla_v Z \rangle,
$$

where $v \langle Y, Z \rangle$ is the derivative at $x$ in the direction $v$ of the function
$y \mapsto \langle Y(y), Z(y) \rangle$.

articles.title: Koszul formula
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, modelled with corners on a finite-dimensional
real normed space, whose tangent bundle carries a smooth Riemannian metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot
\rangle$, and let $\nabla$ be a smooth covariant derivative on the tangent bundle of $M$ that is
torsion-free and compatible with the metric. Then for all smooth vector fields $X$, $Y$, $Z$ on
$M$ and every point $x \in M$, evaluating every term at $x$,

$$2 \langle \nabla_X Y, Z \rangle = X \langle Y, Z \rangle + Y \langle X, Z \rangle -
Z \langle X, Y \rangle - \langle X, [Y, Z] \rangle - \langle Y, [X, Z] \rangle +
\langle Z, [X, Y] \rangle,$$

where $\nabla_X Y$ at $x$ is the covariant derivative of $Y$ in the direction $X(x)$,
$X \langle Y, Z \rangle$ at $x$ is the derivative of the function $y \mapsto \langle Y(y), Z(y)
\rangle$ in the direction $X(x)$, and $[\cdot, \cdot]$ is the Lie bracket of vector fields.

## Sources

- J.-L. Koszul (course notes, 1950s); cf. do Carmo, Riemannian Geometry. Listed as §38 additional statement in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `koszul_formula` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Levi-Civita connection of a vector space is the Fréchet derivative
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space with its standard Riemannian metric, let $V$ be a
vector field on $F$ and $x \in F$, and suppose $V$ is differentiable at $x$ as a section of the
tangent bundle. Then for every tangent vector $v \in T_xF$, the covariant derivative $\nabla_v V$
of $V$ at $x$ for the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ equals $DV(x)(v)$, the Fréchet derivative
of $V$ at $x$ applied to $v$.

articles.title: Fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry (Levi-Civita)
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff smooth
manifold, possibly with boundary or corners, modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space,
whose tangent bundle carries a smooth Riemannian metric. Then there is a smooth covariant
derivative $\nabla$ on the tangent bundle of $M$ that is torsion-free and compatible with the
metric, and every smooth, torsion-free, metric-compatible covariant derivative $\nabla'$ on the
tangent bundle of $M$ agrees with $\nabla$ on smooth vector fields: $\nabla'_v Y = \nabla_v Y$ for
every smooth vector field $Y$ on $M$, every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v$ at $x$.

## Sources

- T. Levi-Civita, Nozione di parallelismo in una varietà qualunque, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 42 (1917). Listed as §38 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `levi_civita_exists_unique` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Agreement of covariant derivatives on smooth vector fields
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold,
possibly with boundary or corners, modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, whose
tangent bundle carries a smooth Riemannian metric. Two covariant derivatives $\nabla$ and
$\nabla'$ on the tangent bundle of $M$ agree on smooth sections when $\nabla_v Y = \nabla'_v Y$
for every smooth vector field $Y$ on $M$, every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v$ at
$x$.

Covariant derivatives here act on all sections of the tangent bundle, not only smooth ones, so the
uniqueness in the Levi-Civita theorem is stated as agreement on smooth vector fields.

articles.title: Mostow rigidity, algebraic form
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 3$, and let $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ be lattices
in the projective orthogonal group $\mathrm{PO}(n,1)$: discrete subgroups that have a fundamental
domain for their action by left multiplication and finite covolume with respect to Haar measure.
Then every group isomorphism $f : \Gamma \to \Lambda$ is a conjugation: there is
$g \in \mathrm{PO}(n,1)$ such that $f(\gamma) = g \gamma g^{-1}$ for all $\gamma \in \Gamma$.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostow_rigidity_theorem#Algebraic_form and Gopal Prasad, *Strong rigidity of ℚ-rank 1 lattices*, Invent. Math. 21 (1973), 255–286. Problem `mostow_rigidity` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Projective indefinite orthogonal group
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, let $J$ be the
diagonal $(p+q) \times (p+q)$ real matrix whose first $p$ diagonal entries are $1$ and whose last
$q$ are $-1$, and let $\mathrm{O}(p,q)$ be the group of real $(p+q) \times (p+q)$ matrices $A$
with $J A^{\mathsf{T}} J A = A J A^{\mathsf{T}} J = I$. The group $\mathrm{PO}(p,q)$ is the
quotient of $\mathrm{O}(p,q)$ by its center.

articles.title: Gaussian potentials that are gradient Ricci solitons
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a real inner product
space of positive finite dimension, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its
inner product, and let $a, c \in \mathbb{R}$. The function $f(x) = \frac{a}{2} \|x\|^2$ on $F$ is
a gradient Ricci soliton with constant $c$ if and only if $a = c$.

articles.title: The Gaussian gradient Ricci soliton
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product
space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and let
$a \in \mathbb{R}$. The function $f(x) = \frac{a}{2} \|x\|^2$ on $F$ is a gradient Ricci soliton
with constant $a$.

For $a < 0$ this is the expanding Gaussian soliton.

articles.title: Gradient Ricci soliton
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (possibly with boundary or corners)
modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, with a smooth Riemannian metric $g$. A
function $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ form a gradient Ricci soliton
if $f$ is smooth and, for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_x(u, v) + (\operatorname{Hess} f)_x(u, v) = c \, g_x(u, v)$, where
$\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature of $g$ and $\operatorname{Hess} f$ is the covariant
Hessian of $f$.

Completeness and connectedness of $M$ are not part of this predicate; they are separate
hypotheses on $M$.

## Sources

- Oberwolfach Report 27/2012 (Geometrie): T. Yokota, p. 1651, defines a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton by `Ric(g) + Hess f = g / (2 * λ)` with `λ > 0` and `f` smooth, and R. Haslhofer (with R. Müller), p. 1669, eq. (1), uses `Rc + Hess f` equal to `g / 2`.

articles.title: Gaussian potentials that are gradient shrinking Ricci solitons
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a real inner
product space of positive finite dimension, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given
by its inner product, and let $a, c \in \mathbb{R}$. The function $f(x) = \frac{a}{2} \|x\|^2$ on
$F$ is a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant $c$ if and only if $a = c$ and $c > 0$.

articles.title: The Gaussian shrinking soliton
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space,
viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and let $a > 0$. The
function $f(x) = \frac{a}{2} \|x\|^2$ on $F$ is a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with
constant $a$.

## Sources

- Oberwolfach Report 27/2012 (Geometrie), T. Yokota, p. 1652; for `a = 1 / 2` this is the Gaussian shrinker `(ℝⁿ, g_E, ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)`.

articles.title: Gradient shrinking Ricci soliton
articles.statement:
On a Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$, a function
$f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ form a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton
if they form a gradient Ricci soliton and $c > 0$.

Completeness and connectedness of $M$ are not part of this predicate.

## Sources

- Oberwolfach Report 27/2012 (Geometrie). In Yokota's notation (p. 1651) this is `c = 1 / (2 * λ)` with `λ > 0`; Haslhofer's normalization (p. 1669, eq. (1)) is `c = 1 / 2`.

articles.title: The Hessian on Euclidean space is the second derivative
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional
real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner
product, let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $x \in F$. If the Fréchet derivative
$y \mapsto Df(y)$ of $f$ is differentiable at $x$, then for all tangent vectors $u, v$ at $x$,
identified with vectors of $F$, the Hessian of $f$ at $x$ is the second Fréchet derivative:
$\nabla^2 f(u, v) = D^2 f(x)(u)(v)$, where $D^2 f(x)$ is the derivative of $Df$ at $x$.

articles.title: The Hessian on Euclidean space as an iterated directional derivative
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a Riemannian manifold with the metric
given by its inner product, let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $x \in F$. For all tangent vectors
$u, v$ at $x$, identified with vectors of $F$, the Hessian of $f$ at $x$ is the derivative at $x$
in direction $u$ of the function $y \mapsto Df(y)(v)$, where $Df(y)$ is the Fréchet derivative of
$f$ at $y$: $\nabla^2 f(u, v) = D\big(y \mapsto Df(y)(v)\big)(x)(u)$.

A Fréchet derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$, so no hypothesis on $f$ is
needed.

articles.title: Covariant Hessian
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional real
normed space, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. For
$f : M \to \mathbb{R}$, a point $x \in M$ and tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xM$, let $V$ be the
extension of $v$ to a vector field with constant coordinates in the preferred chart at $x$, so
that $V(x) = v$. The Hessian of $f$ at $x$ is the real number

$$\nabla^2 f(u, v) = d\big(y \mapsto df_y(V(y))\big)_x(u) - df_x(\nabla_u V),$$

that is, $u(Vf) - df_x(\nabla_u V)$, where $df_y$ is the differential of $f$ at $y$.

This is the textbook Hessian $\nabla^2 f = \nabla(df)$, $\nabla^2 f(u, v) = (\nabla_u df)(v)$
(Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, 2nd ed., GTM 176, Ch. 4), taken as a function of two tangent vectors.

articles.title: Pairing of the Riemannian gradient with a tangent vector
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold
modelled on a complete real normed space, with a Riemannian metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$,
and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \in M$ and $v \in T_xM$. Then
$\langle \operatorname{grad} f(x), v \rangle = df_x(v)$, where $\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ is the
Riemannian gradient of $f$ at $x$ and $df_x$ is the differential of $f$ at $x$.

articles.title: Norm of the Riemannian gradient
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a complete real
normed space, with a Riemannian metric, and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in M$. With $T_xM$
normed by the metric at $x$, the norm of the Riemannian gradient $\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ equals
the operator norm of the differential $df_x : T_xM \to \mathbb{R}$ of $f$ at $x$:
$\|\operatorname{grad} f(x)\| = \|df_x\|$. This is the quantity $|\nabla f|(x)$.

articles.title: Characterization of the Riemannian gradient
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a
complete real normed space, with a Riemannian metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$, and let
$f : M \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \in M$ and $w \in T_xM$. Then the Riemannian gradient
$\operatorname{grad} f(x)$ equals $w$ if and only if $\langle w, v \rangle = df_x(v)$ for every
$v \in T_xM$, where $df_x$ is the differential of $f$ at $x$.

articles.title: The Riemannian gradient on a Hilbert space
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a real Hilbert space, viewed as
a Riemannian manifold with the metric given by its inner product, and let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$
and $x \in F$. Identifying the tangent space at $x$ with $F$, the Riemannian gradient of $f$ at
$x$ is the Hilbert-space gradient $\nabla f(x)$, the unique vector with
$\langle \nabla f(x), w \rangle = Df(x)(w)$ for all $w \in F$, where $Df(x)$ is the Fréchet
derivative of $f$ at $x$.

articles.title: Riemannian gradient
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a $C^1$ manifold modelled on a complete real normed
space, with a Riemannian metric, and let $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in M$. The Riemannian
gradient $\operatorname{grad} f(x) = (df_x)^\sharp \in T_xM$ is the image of the differential
$df_x$ of $f$ at $x$ under the inverse of the Riesz isomorphism
$T_xM \to (T_xM)^*$, $w \mapsto \langle w, \cdot \rangle$, given by the metric at $x$. It is the
unique tangent vector with $\langle \operatorname{grad} f(x), v \rangle = df_x(v)$ for all
$v \in T_xM$.

articles.title: Existence of Riemannian metrics
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let
$M$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on $E$ (possibly with boundary
or corners). Then $M$ admits a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric on its tangent bundle.

## Sources

- J. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed. existence of Riemannian metrics via partition of unity; also Lee, Riemannian Manifolds; Lean states finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable specialization.

articles.title: Normalized Hausdorff measure
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $X$ be an extended
metric space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. The normalized $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of
$X$ is the measure $\frac{\omega_n}{2^n} \mathcal{H}^n$, where $\omega_n$ is the Lebesgue volume of
the open unit ball of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathcal{H}^n$ is the unnormalized
$n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure, in which a set of diameter $r$ has content $r^n$.

With this normalization it agrees with Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (classically, by the
isodiametric inequality); the case $n = 1$ is checked by the computation of the Riemannian volume
of the real line.

articles.title: The Riemannian volume of the real line is Lebesgue measure
articles.statement:
The Riemannian volume of the
real line $\mathbb{R}$, with its standard Riemannian metric (the usual inner product on each tangent
space) and with its usual distance, which is the Riemannian distance, is Lebesgue measure.

This is a normalization check of the Riemannian volume in dimension one.

articles.title: Riemannian volume
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $I$ be a model
with corners on $E$, and let $M$ be a $C^\infty$ manifold modeled on $I$, so that $M$ has dimension
$n = \dim_{\mathbb{R}} E$. Suppose that $M$ carries a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric and an extended
metric equal to the Riemannian distance (the infimum of the lengths of $C^1$ paths), and is given
its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. The Riemannian volume of $M$ is the normalized $n$-dimensional
Hausdorff measure of $M$.

The manifold and Riemannian hypotheses are not used in the formula; they tie the dimension to the
model of $M$ and restrict the definition to the setting in which, classically, this measure is the
Riemannian volume, given in charts by the density $\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}$ against Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Smoothness of a metric in coordinates
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed
space, let $M$ be a smooth manifold modeled through a model with corners $I : H \to E$, and let
$g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on the tangent bundle of $M$. For every chart $e$ in the maximal
smooth atlas of $M$, the coordinate expression of $g$ in $e$, viewed as a map from $E$ to the
continuous bilinear forms on $E$, is $C^\infty$ on the target of the extended chart $I \circ e$.

articles.title: The $C^k$ topologies on smooth metrics get finer as $k$ grows
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth
manifold and let $k \le k'$ be elements of $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. On the space of
smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$, the $C^{k'}$ topology is finer than the $C^k$ topology.

articles.title: The $C^k$ topology on smooth Riemannian metrics
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modelled
on a real normed space $E$ through a model with corners $I$, and let $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup
\{\infty\}$. For a chart $\varphi$ of the maximal smooth atlas of $M$, write $T_\varphi \subseteq E$
for the target of the extended chart $I \circ \varphi$. The (weak, compact-open) $C^k$ topology on
the space of smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$ is the coarsest topology for which, for every
chart $\varphi$ of the maximal atlas and every natural number $i \le k$, the map sending a
metric $g$ to the $i$-th iterated derivative within $T_\varphi$ of the coordinate expression of
$g$ in $\varphi$ is continuous, where these derivatives carry the topology of uniform
convergence on compact subsets of $T_\varphi$.

For $k = \infty$ this is the $C^\infty$ topology. Every element of the space is a smooth metric,
whatever $k$ is; $k$ only indexes the topology.

## Sources

- Burns-Matveev v2 §8.4 finite-atlas `ε`-balls, v3 §8.3 weak `C^k` topology after Hirsch Ch. II. `k = ⊤` is the `C^∞` topology (smooth, not analytic). The space carries smooth metrics for every `k`, and no chart is chosen. Equality with the finite-atlas `ε`-ball topology on a closed manifold follows by the standard argument (relatively compact chart domains and chain rule).

articles.title: Pointwise formula for a metric in coordinates
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
on the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold $M$ modeled through a model with corners
$I : H \to E$, and let $e$ be an open partial homeomorphism from $M$ to $H$. Write $g^e$ for the
coordinate expression of $g$ in $e$, $\psi$ for the inverse of the extended chart $I \circ e$,
$T$ for the target of $I \circ e$, and $D\psi(x)$ for the derivative of $\psi$ at $x$ within
$T$. Then for all $x, v, w \in E$ we have
$g^e(x)(v, w) = g_{\psi(x)}(D\psi(x)\,v, D\psi(x)\,w)$.

articles.title: Conformal scaling of a metric in coordinates
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on
the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold $M$ modeled through a model with corners $I : H \to E$,
let $u : M \to \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function with $u(p) > 0$ for every $p \in M$, and let $e$
be an open partial homeomorphism from $M$ to $H$. Write $g^e$ for the coordinate expression of
$g$ in $e$ and $\psi$ for the inverse of the extended chart $I \circ e$. Then for every $x \in E$
the coordinate expression of the conformally scaled metric $u g$ satisfies
$(u g)^e(x) = u(\psi(x))\, g^e(x)$.

articles.title: Coordinate expression of a Riemannian metric
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on
the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold $M$ modeled through a model with corners $I : H \to E$,
and let $e$ be an open partial homeomorphism from $M$ to $H$. Write $\psi$ for the inverse of the
extended chart $I \circ e$, $T$ for the target of $I \circ e$, and $D\psi(x)$ for the derivative
of $\psi$ at $x$ within $T$. The coordinate expression of $g$ in $e$ is the field of continuous
bilinear forms on $E$ that assigns to each $x \in E$ the pullback form
$(v, w) \mapsto g_{\psi(x)}(D\psi(x)\,v, D\psi(x)\,w)$.

articles.title: Smooth metrics as elements of $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$
articles.statement:
For a smooth manifold $M$ and
$k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, the identity map is a bijection from the space of smooth
Riemannian metrics on $M$ to $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$, the same space of metrics equipped with the
$C^k$ topology.

articles.title: The space $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$ of smooth metrics with the $C^k$ topology
articles.statement:
For a smooth
manifold $M$ and $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$ is the space of all
smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$, equipped with the $C^k$ topology. It is not the space of
$C^k$ metrics: every element is smooth, and $k$ only indexes the topology.

articles.title: Constant rescalings converge in every $C^k$ topology
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on
$M$, and let $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. Let $l$ be a filter on a type $\alpha$ and let
$c_a > 0$ ($a \in \alpha$) be positive reals with $c_a \to 1$ along $l$. Then the rescaled
metrics $c_a g$ tend to $g$ along $l$ in the $C^k$ topology.

In every chart the coordinate expression of $c_a g$ is $c_a$ times that of $g$, hence so is
each iterated derivative within the chart target, while those derivatives of $g$ are bounded on
each compact subset of the target.

articles.title: Convergence in $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modelled on a real
normed space $E$ through a model with corners $I$, let $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, let
$l$ be a filter on a type $\alpha$, and let $g_a$ ($a \in \alpha$) and $g_0$ be smooth
Riemannian metrics on $M$. For a chart $\varphi$ of the maximal smooth atlas of $M$, write
$T_\varphi \subseteq E$ for the target of the extended chart $I \circ \varphi$. Then $g_a$,
regarded as elements of the space $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$ of smooth metrics with the $C^k$
topology, tend to $g_0$ along $l$ if and only if, for every chart $\varphi$ of the maximal
atlas, every natural number $i \le k$ and every compact set $K \subseteq T_\varphi$, the $i$-th
iterated derivatives within $T_\varphi$ of the coordinate expressions of $g_a$ in $\varphi$
converge uniformly on $K$ along $l$ to the $i$-th iterated derivative within $T_\varphi$ of the
coordinate expression of $g_0$ in $\varphi$.

articles.title: Convergence in the $C^k$ topology on smooth metrics
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
modelled on a real normed space $E$ through a model with corners $I$, let
$k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, let $l$ be a filter on a type $\alpha$, and let $g_a$
($a \in \alpha$) and $g_0$ be smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$. For a chart $\varphi$ of the
maximal smooth atlas of $M$, write $T_\varphi \subseteq E$ for the target of the extended chart
$I \circ \varphi$. Then $g_a$ tends to $g_0$ along $l$ in the $C^k$ topology if and only if, for
every chart $\varphi$ of the maximal atlas, every natural number $i \le k$ and every compact set
$K \subseteq T_\varphi$, the $i$-th iterated derivatives within $T_\varphi$ of the coordinate
expressions of $g_a$ in $\varphi$ converge uniformly on $K$ along $l$ to the $i$-th iterated
derivative within $T_\varphi$ of the coordinate expression of $g_0$ in $\varphi$.

## Sources

- Burns-Matveev v3 §8.3.

articles.title: Riemann curvature of a covariant derivative
articles.statement:
Let $
abla$ be a covariant derivative on the
tangent bundle of a smooth manifold $M$. For vector fields $X, Y, Z$ on $M$, the curvature of
$
abla$ is the vector field
$R(X,Y)Z = 
abla_X 
abla_Y Z - 
abla_Y 
abla_X Z - 
abla_{[X,Y]} Z$, where $[X,Y]$ is the Lie
bracket of $X$ and $Y$.

articles.title: Differentiable sphere theorem
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact, Hausdorff, simply connected smooth
manifold without boundary, of dimension $d \ge 2$, with a smooth Riemannian metric. Suppose $M$
carries a smooth covariant derivative $\nabla$ on its tangent bundle that is torsion-free,
compatible with the metric and strictly quarter-pinched (every sectional curvature at an
orthonormal pair lies in $(1, 4]$). Then $M$ is diffeomorphic to the unit sphere
$S^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ with its standard smooth structure.

## Sources

- S. Brendle & R. Schoen, *Manifolds with 1/4-pinched curvature are space forms*, J. AMS 22 (2009). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §121. Problem `sphere_theorem_differentiable` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Strictly quarter-pinched curvature
articles.statement:
Let $\nabla$ be a covariant derivative on the tangent
bundle of a Riemannian manifold $M$, with curvature $R$. Then $\nabla$ is strictly quarter-pinched
when, for all smooth vector fields $X, Y$ on $M$ and every point $x \in M$ at which $X(x)$ and
$Y(x)$ are orthonormal, the sectional curvature $K = \langle R(X,Y)Y(x), X(x) \rangle$ satisfies
$1 < K \le 4$. The interval $(1, 4]$ is Knill's normalization of strict quarter pinching.

articles.title: Topological sphere theorem
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact, Hausdorff, simply connected smooth
manifold without boundary, of dimension $d \ge 2$, with a smooth Riemannian metric. Suppose $M$
carries a smooth covariant derivative $\nabla$ on its tangent bundle that is torsion-free,
compatible with the metric and strictly quarter-pinched (every sectional curvature at an
orthonormal pair lies in $(1, 4]$). Then $M$ is homeomorphic to the unit sphere
$S^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$.

## Sources

- M. Berger; W. Klingenberg; H. E. Rauch (topological sphere theorem, 1951–1961). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §121. Problem `sphere_theorem_topological` of the lean-eval benchmark.
